concepts.title: Health Beyond Not Falling Sick
concepts.definition: Health means complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease; newspaper headlines about diabetes, obesity, anxiety and loneliness show that health depends on lifestyle and society, not just on germs.
concepts.key_idea: Being healthy needs a sound body, a calm mind and good social connections together.
question_patterns: define health in your own words
why is health more than not falling sick
how do lifestyle headlines like obesity and anxiety relate to health
name the three dimensions of well-being that decide health
why can a person without disease still be called unhealthy
what social factors affect the health of a community

solution_steps.explain: Health covers body, mind and social relations together.
Headlines on diabetes, screen time and loneliness show non-germ causes.
A healthy person must satisfy well-being on all three fronts.

concepts.title: How We Stay Healthy
concepts.definition: Good health is maintained by balanced diet with less oil and sugar, regular physical activity or yoga, adequate sleep, limited screen time, clean habits and a healthy environment; each habit lowers the risk of modern lifestyle disorders.
concepts.key_idea: Diet, exercise, sleep and hygiene act together as daily health insurance.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu103.txt lines 103-223 (how can we stay healthy)
question_patterns: list the daily habits that keep a person healthy
why should oil and sugar be reduced in the diet
how does yoga help concentration and anxiety
what harms can excess screen time cause children
how does regular exercise protect against lifestyle diseases
design a healthy daily routine for a school student

solution_steps.explain: Balanced diet and hydration feed the body without excess oil and sugar.
Exercise, yoga and play build fitness and reduce anxiety.
Adequate sleep, limited screens, clean water and handwashing complete the routine.

concepts.title: Knowing We Are Unwell: Symptoms and Diagnosis
concepts.definition: The body signals illness through symptoms such as fever, pain, fatigue or rash; noticing these signs early, checking vital signs and consulting health workers helps identify the disease before it worsens.
concepts.key_idea: Symptoms are the body's alarm; early reading of them makes treatment easier.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu103.txt lines 223-240 (how do we know we are unwell)
question_patterns: how does the body indicate that we are unwell
name three common symptoms of illness
why should symptoms not be ignored
what is the role of a doctor when symptoms appear
how do vital signs help in knowing health status
distinguish a symptom from a disease

solution_steps.explain: Fever, pain, weakness or skin changes mark a departure from normal functioning.
Temperature, pulse and other checks confirm that something is wrong.
Early consultation with health workers leads to correct diagnosis.

concepts.title: Diseases: Causes and Types
concepts.definition: Diseases arise from many causes - germs, poor diet, polluted air, genetic factors or faulty lifestyle - and are grouped as communicable diseases that spread from person to person, like malaria and dengue in the monsoon, and non-communicable diseases like diabetes and heart disease that do not spread.
concepts.key_idea: Communicable diseases travel through agents; non-communicable ones build up from lifestyle and body factors.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu103.txt lines 240-597 (causes and types of diseases)
question_patterns: differentiate communicable and non-communicable diseases with examples
why do malaria and dengue increase in the monsoon
name the causative agents of diseases
how does air pollution act as a cause of disease
why are diabetes and heart attack common in South-east Asia
classify the given diseases into communicable and non-communicable

solution_steps.explain: Germs, diet, pollution, genes or lifestyle may start a disease.
Spreading diseases need an agent and a route; lifestyle diseases stay with the individual.
Monsoon brings mosquito diseases; diet patterns shape diabetes risk.

concepts.title: Prevention and Control of Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases are fought before and after they appear: vaccination builds immunity, clean water and regular handwashing cut infection - by about half - mosquito control checks monsoon diseases, and early screening plus treatment controls the rest.
concepts.key_idea: Prevention through hygiene and vaccines costs less than cure.
question_patterns: how does regular handwashing reduce infection
what is the role of vaccination in disease control
how can mosquito-borne diseases be prevented in the monsoon
list methods of preventing communicable diseases
why is early detection important in controlling disease
suggest a community plan to reduce lifestyle diseases

solution_steps.explain: Clean water, sanitation and handwashing stop germ transmission.
Vaccines prepare the body against specific diseases.
Screening, timely medicine and health education complete the control programme.
